scope: Theorem 5.1 (Local orbit density) of the manuscript “Stabilizer orbits and thick tensor ideals of dualizable K(n)-local spectra” (preprints/Stabilizer-Orbits-and-Thick-Tensor-Ideals-of-Dualizable-Kn-Local-Spectra-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 311 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 5daea14863444214), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 22. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix 1 ≤ h < n and a C-valued point x of the parameter polydisc Ih = 0 with uh(x) ̸= 0. For g ∈ A× n , write yg for its orbit point, with the transport convention of Lemma 4.10. Let G be any open subgroup of A× n . If an analytic germ P at x on the parameter polydisc defined by Ih = 0 vanishes at all points of the orbit {yg : g ∈ G} sufficiently close to x, then P = 0. It suffices to assume that, for every d ∈ An, P(y1−pN d) = 0 for all sufficiently large N.
